transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I just don’t care about the things I used to love doing anymore, even my projects in the garage and going out on the river. I used to spend all my free time working with my hands or being out on the water, but now I just can't bring myself to do any of it.
Have you experienced these feelings of losing interest before in your life, or is this the first time you have felt this way?

No, I've never felt like this before in my life. I’ve always been a steady, active guy who loved singing in the church choir and working on my woodworking projects or fixing up guitars. But ever since that big restructuring at the warehouse about two or three years ago, I just haven't been the same.

Since this started two or three years ago, have these feelings of low mood and loss of interest been present almost every day, or have there been periods where you felt completely like your old self again?

It has been pretty much every single day for the last two years, just this constant heavy feeling. I haven't had any times where I felt like my old self again, because that cloud has never really lifted.

Besides the loss of interest, have you been experiencing other symptoms like significant changes in your appetite, sleep patterns, energy levels, or feelings of worthlessness during these past two years?

Yes, I've lost my appetite and dropped a lot of weight, and I lie awake staring at the ceiling or waking up constantly throughout the night. My body feels incredibly heavy and slow, like my legs are made of concrete, and I can't shake this feeling that I've ruined everything and am just dragging my family down.

To help me understand the severity of your symptoms, are you still able to function at work or perform basic daily tasks, or has your condition made it impossible to carry out your normal responsibilities?

I'm barely scraping by at work, and I've already gotten written up for safety issues and had to turn down extra hours. I've stopped going to church and family gatherings altogether because I just can't face anyone. My wife has to stay on me for everything now, even reminding me to eat and keeping track of our bills.

Have you ever felt so overwhelmed or hopeless that you have experienced delusions, such as believing you have committed unforgivable sins or that your body is physically decaying, or have you experienced any hallucinations?

I haven't had thoughts about unforgivable sins or my body decaying, but I do hear a man's voice behind me telling me I'm dangerous and going to kill someone. I'm also convinced the company put tracking devices in the forklifts and my badge to watch me and wait for me to screw up. These strange things and the voices have been happening right alongside that heavy, hopeless feeling the whole time.
In the years before this current two-year period began, did you ever experience any other distinct episodes of feeling this depressed, or was your mood consistently stable and normal prior to this?
I don't recall ever feeling this way before in my life. Before the warehouse restructuring started about three years ago, I was always a very steady, active, and competitive person.

Looking back at your life before this current two-year period, can you confirm with certainty that you never had any other distinct, separate periods where you felt this depressed or unable to function?

Yes, I can confirm that with absolute certainty. Before the warehouse restructuring about three years ago, I was always my usual steady, competitive self and never had any issues like this. This is the very first time in my life that I've ever felt so depressed or struggled to function.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets the criteria for a major depressive episode of severe intensity, characterized by persistent low mood, anhedonia, somatic symptoms (weight loss, insomnia, psychomotor retardation), feelings of worthlessness, and functional impairment. Crucially, the presence of auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions (tracking devices) occurring concurrently with the depressive symptoms supports a diagnosis of major depressive disorder with psychotic features.
